content.user_title: Review a Chrome Website Decluttering Extension Guide
content.value_statement: Planning a website decluttering extension requires clear feature requirements and development constraints. This public guide describes a no-build Manifest V3 approach, but does not include implementation files.
actual_capabilities: Describes a Manifest V3 extension approach using vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
Lists intended clutter categories, including popups, chat widgets, sticky headers, and social sidebars.
Explains the intended use of chrome.storage for preferences and restoration states.
Outlines manual extension reloading and the Chrome Load unpacked development workflow.
Documents heuristic detection and the stated exclusion of iframe and Shadow DOM content.
limitations: Only a Markdown guide is included; extension source, scripts, and templates are absent.
Production readiness, Chrome Web Store acceptance, and complete reversibility are claims, not verified results.
The described detection is heuristic and does not cover elements inside iframes or Shadow DOM.
The described development workflow requires manual extension reloading after edits.

use_cases.title: Learn extension development concepts
use_cases.description: Review the documented no-build approach, Manifest V3 terminology, and manual reload workflow before starting an extension project.

use_cases.title: Define decluttering requirements
use_cases.description: Use the listed clutter categories, preference storage, and restoration goals to draft requirements for a separately implemented browser utility.

use_cases.title: Plan extension validation
use_cases.description: Translate the guide's heuristic detection, restoration claims, and iframe exclusions into a test checklist for source obtained separately.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this skill's guide in plain language. Distinguish documented extension features from files actually included in this package.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the development workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the no-build Manifest V3 workflow described in this guide. Identify the source files I must obtain before using Chrome's Load unpacked option.

prompt_templates.title: Draft implementation requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn the guide into requirements for a separately implemented extension. Cover clutter categories, reversible hiding, preferences, and unsupported DOM contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a verification plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a validation plan for the described extension. Include dynamic pages, restoration, stored preferences, permission review, and iframe exclusions. Mark unverified claims.

output_examples.input: What does this package actually include?
output_examples.output: The package contains a Markdown guide. It describes a decluttering extension, but includes no extension source, executable scripts, or templates.

output_examples.input: Which constraints should inform my test plan?
output: Check heuristic detection for missed clutter and unintended hiding.
Treat iframe and Shadow DOM content as unsupported by the described design.
Verify restoration and preference persistence against separately obtained source.
Reload the unpacked extension manually after source changes.

output_examples.input: Can I load this package directly into Chrome?
output_examples.output: No. The extension source and manifest are absent. Obtain and review an implementation before loading it as an unpacked extension.

best_practices: Confirm which implementation files are available before planning installation or publication.
Review extension permissions and source before loading any separately obtained implementation.
Test detection and restoration across representative sites before relying on the guide's compatibility claims.
anti_patterns: Treating this documentation package as an installable extension.
Reporting the guide's example output as files actually generated or included.
Assuming heuristic hiding guarantees intact layouts or complete reversibility on every website.

faq.question: Does this package include a working Chrome extension?
faq.answer: No. The guide explicitly states that extension source, scripts, and templates from the original package are not included.

faq.question: What does the guide describe?
faq.answer: It describes a no-build Manifest V3 extension intended to hide website clutter and store user preferences.

faq.question: Are Node.js or build tools required?
faq.answer: The described architecture uses vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without build tools. No implementation is available here to verify that setup.

faq.question: Can the described extension handle iframes or Shadow DOM?
faq.answer: The guide lists elements inside iframes and Shadow DOM as unsupported.

faq.question: Is Chrome Web Store readiness verified?
faq.answer: No. The guide claims production readiness, but this package has no implementation or test results to verify publication readiness.

faq.question: Why does the example claim that source was generated?
faq.answer: That passage is an illustrative result in the guide. It does not establish that source files exist in this package.
